newsitem.title: UK: Nomura strategist ups FTSE 100 index targets.
newsitem.headline: Nomura strategist ups FTSE 100 index targets.

text.p: Nomura equity strategist Nick Knight said on Wednesday he had raised his year-end targets for the FTSE 100 index, reflecting hopes that inflation and interest rates will stay low through the rest of the year.
For the end of 1996 he upped his target to 4,800 from 4,400 and for the end of 1997 he moved to 5,200 from 4,800.

Knight said stocks should be able to make further progress against the background of the so-called "goldilocks" economy, where economic growth was strong enough for company earnings to prosper yet not so strong as to generate inflation.
"We could even get a very nice scenario where sterling strength is enough to dampen inflation without really damaging domestic growth," he said.
"We cannot really see an end to the Goldilocks scenario over the foreseeable future."

Knight said his FTSE 100 forecasts assumed that gilt yields would dip to seven percent by year end and assumed a gilt-equity yield ratio, a commonly used measure that compares the return on gilts to that on equities, of just over two times.
